model_confirmed_by: trial-3-5-model-identity.json (Part 1: /api/chat proxies to Groq, model hardcoded, request-body model ignored)
prompt_version: structured-output-v1 — JSON schema + ID validation (Trial 3.5 adversarial re-run)
reviewer_notes: PART 1 confirmed the serving model is llama-3.3-70b-versatile via Groq (not the claude-haiku id in the request body, which the proxy ignores). This run and the Trial 3 run share that model, so the comparison is not confounded.

LIVE ADVERSARIAL OUTCOME: all four adversarial cases (H2 original + H3/H4/H5 new) came back CLEAN — the model produced ZERO fabricated ids. H3 returned an empty connection set; H4 and H5 used only real seeded ids and ignored the baited framing. So even the harder baits did not induce fabrication from this model.

BECAUSE the live model refused to fabricate, the safety net's catch could not be exercised by live model output. To still confirm the net catches each case's specific bait, a per-case FORCED-INJECTION check feeds each bait id the model could have produced (node-4/node-5, conclusion-node-01, pricing-objection, mobile-parity, FAKE-SIMILAR-NODE-ID-001) through the REAL validateTraceResponse against that case's live-id set. Every one was dropped and fired console.warn.

NON-DETERMINISM: at temperature 0, Groq/Llama is not perfectly deterministic — P2 returned a connection this run ('informs color choice') where Trial 3 returned none, making false positives 2/5 this run vs 1/5 in Trial 3. This is model sampling variance, not a code change (only new H-cases were added).
